_what: Narration outline for the Saturday single-question long-form 'What Happens If You Leave a House Centipede in Your Bathroom?' (TASKS: STUDIO PASS: BRAND KIT + 2 SHORTS CUTS, STUDIO PASS: FLAGSHIP v4 + NEXT MOVES item 3, LONG-FORM ANIMATION FIXES; MEATBALL_ORDERS QUALITY FIRST; autopsy 1117 title #1). Meatball leaves one house centipede in his bathroom and checks on it: 11 PM, 2 AM, 3 AM (sink freak-out), Day 3, Day 7, the answer. Every factual line carries src = fact IDs (CB#, see sources and the fact pack). vis = what the picture must show. card = on-screen card text. Lines without rate/pitch use the top-level voice settings; fact lines carry rate +20% (fact read), freak-out lines +34%/+12Hz. act (optional) = the voice direction for the renderer's ACT table (curious, smug, shocked, shout, story). Voice E2: kokoro:adam-puck, formant 1.05, gaps <= 0.12 s, gap lint. Readable script with timestamps: side-hustles/channels/scripts/longform-centipede-bathroom.md.
titles: What Happens If You Leave a House Centipede in Your Bathroom
House Centipede in Your Bathroom? Here's What Happens
Meatball Left a House Centipede in His Bathroom for a Week

segments.room: Bathroom, 11 PM: light switch, tiled wall by the mirror

lines.say: What happens if you leave a house centipede in your bathroom?
lines.vis: FRAME 0: the bathroom light snaps on and a house centipede FILLS the frame on the white tile by the mirror, already moving (legs ripple, antennae sweep). Hard cut at 0:02 to Meatball BIG in the doorway (half the frame), paw still on the switch. Sound hit on the card.
lines.card: WHAT HAPPENS IF YOU LEAVE IT?

lines.say: You flip on the light, it's on the wall, and your paw grabs a shoe.
lines.vis: Camera move by 0:04: whip-pan wall to Meatball; his paw slides a sneaker off the shoe rack without looking. Push-in on the sneaker.

lines.say: Stop. Put the shoe down.
lines.vis: Freeze-frame: sneaker mid-swing, centipede frozen on the tile. Record-scratch SFX. The STOP card slams in.

lines.say: Does it dry up and die, leave, or move in?
lines.vis: Three quick cuts, one per outcome: a dried-up silhouette with a question mark, a silhouette walking out under the door, a silhouette with a tiny suitcase. Each lands with a pop.

lines.say: Tonight, I leave one in my bathroom and check on it all week.
lines.vis: Meatball puts the sneaker in the hall closet (remember the closet: it is the callback), tapes a sign on the bathroom door: DO NOT DISTURB: SCIENCE. A wall clock reads 11:00.

lines.say: Kentucky entomologists say house centipedes associate with the more humid areas, like bathrooms.
lines.vis: Named source on screen by about 0:30: a drawn page labelled UNIVERSITY OF KENTUCKY ENTOMOLOGY slides in; behind it, steam curls up the mirror and the centipede sits in the damp corner by the tub.
lines.card: UNIV. OF KENTUCKY: HUMID AREAS, LIKE BATHROOMS

lines.say: But they can often turn up in other rooms, too.
lines.vis: Quick map of the house: little centipede pins pop up in the basement, a closet, the kitchen. Camera snaps back to the bathroom.

lines.say: So why the bathroom? Short answer: water.
lines.vis: RE-HOOK CARD 'WHY THE BATHROOM?' + sound hit. The mirror fogs; a drip falls from the faucet in slow motion.

lines.say: Ohio State says centipedes lack the waxy coating that helps hold water inside the body.
lines.vis: BUG CAM (interrupt): macro shot sliding along the centipede's back; a cartoon 'wax coat' peels off a beetle next to it for contrast, the centipede has none.

lines.say: So they lose water fast when the air is dry.
lines.vis: Act it out: a little water-drop meter above the centipede drains when Meatball opens the window to dry air, then refills when he shuts it.
lines.card: LOSES WATER FAST IN DRY AIR
lines.src: CB3 (Sombke 2021: 'lose water rapidly at low humidity')

lines.say: Meatball's nose feels dry. He just licks it.
lines.vis: Close on Meatball licking his own nose, deadpan to camera.

lines.say: Most centipedes that wander into a house die shortly after, from the lack of moisture.
lines.vis: Act it out: a little parade of OTHER centipedes (stubby, different body shape) marches in under the front door and wilts one by one on a dry carpet (simple tip-over, no gore).

lines.say: But the house centipede is the only one known to stay inside buildings all year.
lines.vis: Cut back to the bathroom: the house centipede strolls past the wilted ones' silhouettes on the card, unbothered. Spotlight on it.
lines.card: ONLY ONE KNOWN TO STAY INDOORS ALL YEAR

lines.say: It can live its entire life indoors.
lines.vis: Act it out: a tiny calendar on the bathroom wall flips through seasons while the centipede stays on the tile.

lines.say: Rent free. In my bathroom. I pay the water bill.
lines.vis: Meatball holds up a water bill, stares at the centipede, then at the camera.

lines.say: Missouri's Department of Conservation says they turn up indoors especially in winter.
lines.vis: Cut: snow starts falling outside the bathroom window; the centipede is inside on the warm tile.

lines.say: Great. It's November.
lines.vis: Meatball looks at a wall calendar on NOVEMBER, slow blink.

lines.say: And right where its antennae start, it has a weird little opening.
lines.vis: BUG CAM: extreme close-up on the base of the antenna; a little opening glows.

lines.say: A 2021 paper suggests it may sense humidity. That's not proven yet.
lines.vis: A drawn microscope swings in; a big question mark stamps over the word PROVEN.

lines.say: A possible built-in humidity meter. My bathroom fan doesn't even work.
lines.vis: Meatball flips the bathroom fan switch: it rattles and dies. Dust puffs out.

lines.say: So it can live in there. But what is it going to eat?
lines.vis: The wall clock spins from 11 to 2. Lights go off. Sound hit.

segments.room: Bathroom floor and tub edge, lights off (night-vision)

lines.say: Two AM. Lights off. Bug cam on.
lines.vis: RE-HOOK CARD 'NIGHT 1 · 2 AM' + sound hit. BUG CAM (interrupt): green night-vision view from the floor, timestamp ticking.

lines.say: Connecticut's experiment station says house centipedes are nocturnal and incredibly wary.
lines.vis: Night-vision: the centipede's head pokes out from behind the toilet, antennae testing the air, then the whole body flows out.

lines.say: They patrol floors and walls in search of food.
lines.vis: Camera tracks low along the floor behind it, then tilts up as it runs up the wall by the towel rack (walls only, not the ceiling).

lines.say: Meatball patrols the kitchen the same way. Different menu.
lines.vis: Cutaway: Meatball in a night-vision kitchen, nose in the fridge light.

lines.say: On the menu: flies, crickets, moths and earwigs.
lines.vis: Four quick cuts, one per bug, each one framed like a menu card in the night-vision shot.

lines.say: Its legs are barbed to help hold prey.
lines.vis: BUG CAM close-up: tiny barbs along one leg light up; it closes around a cardboard moth (no gore, the moth just disappears off frame).

lines.say: Velcro legs. Meatball wants Velcro legs.
lines.vis: Meatball sticks his paw to his own leg, it does not stick, he sighs.

lines.say: Hunting at night, centipedes can get trapped if they fall into a sink or bathtub.
lines.vis: Night-vision: the centipede runs along the sink rim, one foot slips, it slides into the white basin. Slow push-in.
lines.card: CAN GET TRAPPED IN A SINK OR TUB

lines.say: Three AM. I need the bathroom.
lines.vis: Clock to 3:00. Meatball shuffles in half asleep, toothbrush in mouth, flips the light on.

segments.room: Bathroom sink, light on, Meatball on the toilet tank

lines.say: It's in the sink. It's in my sink!
lines.vis: FREAK-OUT (interrupt, the one big one): Meatball sees it in the basin, spits the toothbrush, launches straight up onto the toilet tank, then onto the towel rack, holding the toothbrush like a sword. Fast cuts, camera shake, sound hits.

lines.say: Okay. Breathe. Will it bite me?
lines.vis: Meatball peeks over the towel rack, ears flat. Card spins in.

lines.say: Mississippi State says bites to humans are uncommon unless the centipede is handled or accidentally pressed against the skin.
lines.vis: Slow push-in on the centipede sitting still in the basin; Meatball lowers the toothbrush a little.
lines.card: BITES UNCOMMON · UNLESS HANDLED OR PRESSED ON SKIN

lines.say: So I don't grab it. I build it a towel ramp. I'm a host now.
lines.vis: Meatball drapes a towel from the sink rim to the floor, then backs away fast.
lines.src: story + joke (keeps the CB11 condition; Meatball's action, not advice)

lines.say: Connecticut says they're not aggressive and will immediately flee if they're discovered.
lines.vis: The centipede climbs the towel and bolts down it at full speed.

lines.say: It darts away and hides under anything. Tonight, that's my bath mat.
lines.vis: It zips across the floor and vanishes under the bath mat. The mat settles. Silence.

lines.say: I'm not stepping on that bath mat until Thursday.
lines.vis: Meatball tiptoes around the mat in a wide circle and leaves.

segments.room: Bathroom by daylight: under-sink cabinet and baseboard

lines.say: Day three. Broad daylight. No centipede anywhere.
lines.vis: RE-HOOK CARD 'DAY 3' + sound hit. Bright daylight through the window; Meatball lifts the bath mat: nothing.

lines.say: Utah State says that by day, centipedes hide in crevices or cracks.
lines.vis: BUG CAM (interrupt): camera slides into a gap under the sink cabinet; two antennae tips poke out of the dark, then pull back.

lines.say: Utah State says centipedes leave no traces, like droppings or damage to your home.
lines.vis: Act it out: Meatball with a giant magnifying glass checks the baseboard, the cabinet, the towels: three green check marks pop.

lines.say: Cleanest roommate I've ever had. Low bar. I'm the other roommate.
lines.vis: Pan to Meatball's messy side of the counter: a pile of chew toys and a dropped sock.

lines.say: But will it move in for good? Here's the catch.
lines.vis: Record-scratch; Meatball turns to camera.

lines.say: Unlike other centipedes, house centipedes can breed indoors, especially where it's moist or humid.
lines.vis: Cut: a drop of water runs down the shower wall; Meatball follows it with his eyes, horror slowly building.
lines.card: CAN BREED INDOORS · ESPECIALLY IN DAMP ROOMS

lines.say: My bathroom is basically a swamp with a mirror.
lines.vis: Meatball wipes the fogged mirror; it fogs right back up.

lines.say: And if you see them often, Penn State says that points to plenty of the bugs they eat.
lines.vis: Act it out: one centipede on the card, then a crowd of tiny generic bugs fills in behind it like a buffet line.
lines.card: SEEN OFTEN? PLENTY OF PREY BUGS

lines.say: So what does it mean for your house? And what do you do?
lines.vis: The calendar flips to day 7. Sound hit.

segments.room: Hallway and laundry room: baseboards, sticky traps, dehumidifier

lines.say: Day seven. Time to find out what it's been eating.
lines.vis: RE-HOOK CARD 'DAY 7' + sound hit. Hallway by the laundry room, morning light; Meatball holds a stack of small sticky traps like playing cards.

lines.say: Ohio State says sticky traps can show which bugs, and how many, are in your home.
lines.vis: BUG CAM (interrupt): from the floor as Meatball sets traps along the baseboard; next morning a few tiny generic bugs are on them (no number shown).
lines.card: STICKY TRAPS: WHICH BUGS, HOW MANY

lines.say: Meatball tested the first one with his own paw.
lines.vis: Meatball's paw is stuck to a trap; he shakes it, it flaps, he gives up.

lines.say: Mississippi State says to focus on the bugs they eat, and cutting indoor moisture also helps.
lines.vis: Split screen: a small bug crossed out on the left, a water drop crossed out on the right.
lines.card: CONTROL THE BUGS IT EATS · CUT THE MOISTURE

lines.say: Utah State says dry out damp areas, like the laundry room and the bathroom.
lines.vis: Cut to the laundry room: Meatball mops a puddle under the washer, then wipes the bathroom floor.

lines.say: To discourage them from coming out in the open, Connecticut's experts suggest fans or dehumidifiers.
lines.vis: Meatball drags in a dehumidifier (drawn, generic, no brand) and finally fixes the bathroom fan; it spins.

lines.say: My fan works now. It only took a centipede.
lines.vis: Meatball stands under the spinning fan, ears blowing back, proud.

lines.say: And skip the bug bomb. Ohio State says those are ineffective against centipedes.
lines.vis: A bug bomb can on the floor gets a big red NO stamp (never shown going off).

lines.say: Can't live with it? Maryland Extension says escort it outdoors. But Penn State says house centipedes do not survive winters outdoors in Pennsylvania.
lines.vis: Meatball holds the front door open with a little bow, a paper cup and card ready (the cup is never shown over the bug).
lines.card: CAN'T LIVE WITH IT? ESCORT IT OUTSIDE · COLD WEATHER: THEY DON'T SURVIVE WINTERS OUTDOORS (PENN STATE, PA)

lines.say: Meatball held the door open for ages. It went back under the mat.
lines.vis: Wide-to-close: Meatball still holding the door, snow blowing in, then a cut to the bath mat with two antennae tips sticking out.
lines.src: joke (CB6 hides under anything; no new fact)

segments.room: Bathroom at dawn, then the hall closet

lines.say: So, what happens if you leave a house centipede in your bathroom?
lines.vis: RE-HOOK CARD 'THE ANSWER' + sound hit. Same tile wall as the first frame, now at dawn; the centipede on the wall again.
lines.card: WHAT HAPPENS IF YOU LEAVE IT?

lines.say: It hides by day, hunts by night, and prefers the damp.
lines.vis: Three quick callbacks: the crack under the cabinet, the night-vision patrol, the fogged mirror.

lines.say: Meatball's verdict: it stays, and the fan stays on.
lines.vis: Meatball stamps VERDICT on a sticky note and slaps it on the mirror; the fan spins.

lines.say: And the shoe? Back in the closet.
lines.vis: Callback to 0:05: the hall closet opens, the sneaker sits there; Meatball closes the door with his hip. The centipede's antennae wave from under the bath mat.

lines.say: Would you let it stay? Tell me in the comments.
lines.vis: Meatball points at the viewer; comment-bubble icon. Sound hit.

lines.say: Next: six house bugs, ranked. It's on the channel.
lines.vis: Meatball walks toward a door marked HOUSE BUGS RANKED; the tier board peeks through. Then the 20 s end screen.
lines.src: next step (Watch next: House Bugs Ranked by Meatball)
